subtitle: Midterm Important MCQs

mcqs.question: The study of various processes used in the production of the speech sound is known as ___________ phonetics.
Phonemes are abstract entities while ________ are the physical realizations of phonemes.
How many sub-types does phonology have?
Phonology is the study of the ______ structure of language.
The _____ component provides a detailed analysis and description of speech sounds with particular emphasis on articulatory phonetics.
The ______ component examines the internal structure of simplex and complex word forms.
In ______ words are arranged into a certain order.
In ____, beginnings and endings of the words are changed to adjust the meaning.
Through ____, the meaning itself can be affected by the arrangement of words.
The branch of linguistics in which the knowledge of the speaker about what the hearer will understand is used is _____.
Sets of phonemes and sound patterns are dynamic; as in ______ speech.
Sets of phonemes and sound patterns are ______ as in isolation within a human language.
Which of the following are NOT pulmonic sounds?

The 'glottalic' airstream mechanism uses the movement of the ________.
VOT stands for ________.

Simple unaspirated voiceless stops have a voice onset time at or near ________.
When the air moves outwards from the body, it is called ________ airstream.
The air is allowed to escape freely as vocal folds open apart during the process of ________.
What is another name for larynx?
Almost all the sounds we produce in speaking are created with the help of air compressed by the ________.
The velaric airstream mechanism involves an airstream produced by a movement of the back of the tongue against the ______.
Lower articulators are ________.
Which of the following sounds does NOT fall under the category of obstruents?
The production of nasal sound due to the air pressure diversion from oral cavity towards nasal cavity is known as ___________ process.
The phenomenon of articulators interacting with each other is termed as ________.
First sound in 'yes' is _____.
Nasals, liquids and glides fall under the category of ________.
In the production of a fricative sound, which of the following is NOT true about the air passage?
options: It stops air and suppressed sound is produced.
It allows air to pass with a hiss.

mcqs.question: The terms ________ are specifically used in the phonetic classification of consonantal sounds on the basis of their manners of articulation.
When two sounds are articulated together, it is known as __________.
According to rules for English Consonantal Allophones(ECA), approximants /w, r, j, l/ are ________ after initial /p, t, k/ sounds, as in play, twin, etc.
The factor of the full/partial blockage of air passage is discussed in the ________ of articulation.
When air is released through very narrow air passage creating friction and hissing in human larynx then ________ are produced.
In velarisation of sound, which of the following articulators plays an active role?
In English language, fricatives are also known as ________.
Vowels, nasals and approximants are usually ________ sounds.
According to the descriptive rules of consonants, the consonants at the end of the phrase will be________.
The air escaping through nasal cavity results in the production of ________ sounds.
In English there are ________ stop consonant sounds.
Which of the following sounds are easily distinguishable using the voicing features?
Nasalization is a result of ________ process where air is allowed to go through nasal cavity.
When the vocal folds are apart, the resultant sounds are called ________.
In English stop consonant sounds /p/ and /b/ are labeled as ________ sounds.
Which part of the tongue does the term 'laminal' represent?
In the production of a plosive like [p], which of the following is not a sub-task?
In the production of [p] sound, which of the following tasks occupies the top node?
The features [voiceless] and [breathy voice] are studied under the cover term ________.
In addition to create a voiceless bilabial (i.e. [p]), the glottis needs to be ________.
/b/ and /d/ fall under the category of ______ sounds.
Human sounds are divided into ___ broad categories.
A consonant is a speech sound in which air is at least ______ blocked.
______ is a sound in which there is no obstruction found and the air passes through the cavity freely.
A ________ is classified in terms of the places and manners of articulation and voicing.
During the production of vowels, the articulators _________.
options: air is restricted at several points

mcqs.question: Lower overtones (F1) tell us about the ________.
By default, all vowels are ________.
Acoustically, vowels are mainly distinguished by the first _____ formant frequencies.
Which of the following is always at the nucleus position of the syllables?
Vowels are ______ in syllables closed by a nasal consonant.
The RP (Received Pronunciation) accent of English has ________ vowels.
Vowels tend to be ________ in the stressed syllables.
The vowel /i/ is a ________ vowel.
Diphthong is a single vowel consisting of the features of ________.
The idea of cardinal vowels was given by ___________.
Lax sounds are produced with ________ muscular effort and movement.
A vowel may take one out of three forms: stressed, unstressed and ________.
In the articulation of /u/ sound, the tongue is at ________ position.
Many of the ______ vowels are essentially different than those of British and that is why it is a different English.
The vowel(s) used in the words 'beer', 'loud' and 'time' can be characterized as _________.
/ɜː/ and /ɑː/ are examples of ______ vowels.
A vowel is classified in terms of the position of tongue, the part of tongue and ____.
Vowels are further classified into two types: pure vowels and ______.
Pure vowels are known as _______.
Which one of the following is NOT true for IPA charts?
options: IPA charts are never changed since they were first made
IPA charts guide for vowels as well as consonants
IPA charts provide symbols for all languages of the world

Citation speech is the one where word is in its ________ form.

Linguists, speech engineers and speech pathologists focus upon sound ______ in terms of sound hearing.
The waveforms of consonants can inform us about the __________.
Which of the following keyboard keys will be useful to 'paste' the copied or 'print screen' image on a word document?
F0 should be taken from the ________ of a sound.
While confirming the pitch measurements, one should see the ________ peak of the spectral slice.
Harmonics are basically the result of the ________ vibration.
While measuring pitch manually, one should click in the middle of the ________.
Harmonics are the multiple integers of the ________ which are basically the result of vocal fold vibration.
In order to have the spectral make-up of the vowels, we need to take the formant values (for first ________ formant/s).
Praat software is particularly useful for ________ analysis.
Which of the following is the safest way for pitch measurement?
In order to name your sound file, you have to click on which of the following buttons?
While recording on Praat, if you are too loud to go into the red in the volume bar, you will end up with ________.
Pitch measurement can be confirmed by looking at the ________.
What keyboard command is used to remove an unnecessary text-grid boundary on Praat?
In order to describe intonation, we need to analyze the role of a ________.
In typical 'tone' languages, the linguistic function of ________ is to change the meaning of a word.
In the American structuralist tradition, ________ degrees of stress are usually distinguished.
Intonation refers to the ________ in the pitch of a speaker's voice.
Speech is perceived as a sequence of ________ in time.
The 'strong' form is the result of a word being ________.
Stress is a term used in phonetics to refer to the degree of force used in producing a ________.
Choose the right option. Stress on a syllable within a word is called ________ stress.
In Mandarin (Chinese), /ma/ said with high pitch means ________
A word that contains one syllable only is called ________.
Noticeable event occurring at regular intervals
